The West Coast

Barbados at its most unhurried

Carlton Ridge sits within Carlton View Estate, on Barbados’s celebrated West Coast — the stretch of coastline known locally as the Platinum Coast for its calm, reef-sheltered water and long tradition of quiet, well-kept residences. Holetown and Speightstown are both close by, along with the island’s best golf and some of its finest dining.

Holetown

Barbados’s first English settlement, now the West Coast’s most polished address — boutique shopping at Limegrove, waterfront dining, and the Holetown Monument marking where it all began in 1627.

Explore Holetown

Speightstown

A working fishing port turned quiet favourite, its colonial “Little Bristol” architecture giving way to a jetty, an esplanade, and some of the West Coast’s least crowded beaches.

Explore Speightstown

The Beach

Easy access, just a short walk from the villa, to the calm, reef-sheltered water the Platinum Coast is famous for — sea turtles feeding just offshore, and some of the island’s best-loved stretches of sand only minutes away.

Platinum Coast beaches

Where to eat

Our favourite restaurants

A short list of West Coast favourites, from torch-lit fine dining to toes-in-the-sand beach bars — all within easy reach of Carlton Ridge.

Fine dining

Lone Star

A Platinum Coast institution on the beach at Mount Standfast — European and Caribbean flavours, a buzzy see-and-be-seen crowd, and Sunday lunch that’s a local ritual.

Visit website

The Cliff

Barbados’s original fine-dining landmark, its torch-lit terraces built into the rock face above the sea. The restaurant is now led by Michelin-starred chef Matt Worswick.

Visit website

The Cliff Beach House

The Cliff’s easier-going sister on the sand at Derricks — all-day dining, wood-fired pizza and sunset sessions in place of white tablecloths.

Visit website

Baia

Peruvian-fusion cooking on a cliffside beachfront just north of Speightstown, with ceviche, an open charcoal grill and a strong tequila list.

Visit website

The Fishpot

Fresh seafood inside a 17th-century fort on the northwest coast, family-run for over twenty years with an unbeatable view over the bay.

Visit website

Derrière

An authentic French brasserie tucked into Limegrove — steak frites, moules marinières and a proper Parisian wine list, from breakfast through to late.

Visit website

Fusion

Penthouse dining atop Limegrove with a retractable roof and sweeping West Coast views — sophisticated, international, and best after dark.

Visit website

West 101

Gourmet island cooking by day from Chef Michael Hinds, turning into one of Holetown’s liveliest bars by night, right in Limegrove.

Visit website

Beach bars & casual

Sea-Shed

A laid-back beach day spot on Mullins Bay — loungers and cocktails by day, live music and DJs as the evening takes over.

Visit website

La Cabane

Barefoot beach dining on Batts Rock, all swings and hand-painted signs — Mediterranean-Bajan food from the team behind Derrière.

Visit website

Local & Co

Farm-to-table dining, a market and a rum bar inside a lovingly restored 18th-century warehouse on the beach in Speightstown — beautifully done and true to its word.

Visit website

Sand Street Bistro

A relaxed beachfront bistro in the heart of Speightstown, with sunset views across the road from the sand and a well-loved happy hour.

Visit website

Juma’s

Family-friendly, oceanfront dining on Alleynes Bay, two doors up from Lone Star — a Platinum Coast favourite for sunset dinners.

Visit website

Juju’s

Toes-in-the-sand simplicity at Mount Standfast — fresh catch, cold Banks beer and a straightforward menu right on one of the West Coast’s best beaches.

Visit website

Bombas

Farm-to-table, sea-to-table dining right on Mullins Bay — fresh daily catch curated by owner Wayne, with a warm, colourful, laid-back setting.

Visit website

Suggested itinerary

A Stay at Carlton Ridge

A guest itinerary — the best of the West Coast, at your own pace.

Day One

Arrival

Touch down and settle in. Ease into island time on the covered patio with a rum punch as the sun drops over the garden, or take a first dip in the pool before dinner in — the chef’s kitchen can be stocked and ready at your request, so there’s no need to leave the villa on day one.

Day Two

Alleynes Bay

A short drive to Alleynes Bay for a morning on the sand — calm, clear West Coast water, ideal for an easy swim before lunch back at the villa. Afternoon by the pool, sundowners at the wet bar. Dinner at The Fishpot is the perfect way to round off the day.

Day Three

Boat Trip & Snorkelling with Captain Dwayne

A full day on the water with Captain Dwayne’s cruises along the Platinum Coast — snorkelling with turtles and over a shipwreck, with rum punch on tap for the ride home. Pack a swimsuit and sun cream, and keep dinner back at the villa easy after a day in the sun.

Day Four

Limegrove & Lone Star

Late start, then into Holetown for the afternoon — Limegrove Lifestyle Centre for shopping, a browse through the boutiques, maybe lunch out. In the evening, dinner at Lone Star, the famed beachfront restaurant on the Platinum Coast, a short drive from the villa.

Day Five

Friday Night in Oistins

No week in Barbados is complete without Friday night at Oistins — the fish fry, the music, the whole south coast turning out for grilled mahi-mahi and cold beer at communal tables. Loud, local, and one of the best nights on the island.

Day Six

Harrison's Cave

A change of pace inland: Harrison’s Cave for the underground tram tour through Barbados’s limestone caverns — cool, dramatic, and a good contrast to a week by the water. Back at the villa by afternoon for pool time and a quiet evening in.

Day Seven

Sunday at Sea Shed or La Cabane

Round out the week the way Barbados does — a long, easy Sunday at Sea Shed or La Cabane, beachfront dining with your toes in the sand and no particular plan for the afternoon.

Day Eight

Departure day

Last swim, last coffee on the terrace, pack up and go — already planning the next visit.
